short_description:
Who's Lying? #1, the answer: the gardener lied. He said he heard the thunder, then saw the lightning. That's impossible: light travels nearly a million times faster than sound (about 186,000 miles per second vs. about 767 mph), so you always see the flash before you hear the boom. And the maid's tea? A gas stove works fine in a blackout.

Bonus trick: count the seconds between the flash and the thunder. Every 5 seconds is about 1 mile (NOAA / National Weather Service).

Missed the case? Watch it here: https://youtube.com/shorts/sy3cjTLxhQA
New case this Saturday 🕵️

Sources: NOAA National Weather Service, NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory.
